description: Frozen canonical name-normalization example table (migration step 1 of docs/normalization_migration_blocked.md). 'canonical' values are the ruled canonical_v2 policy; 'legacy' values are computed from the current code and pinned by tests/test_canonical_name_examples.py. 'family' is a reviewer-facing category label. 'equivalence_group' means the cases must share identical canonical first/middle/last fields. Case-level 'decisions' are primary review highlights, not exhaustive dependency labels. Count keys use initial_char semantics; null count keys mean no lookup (missing), never sentinel counts. compare_compatibility encodes the compare-time equivalence contract (same_prefix_tokens) across variant groups that are deliberately not canonicalization-identical. compatible_groups are case ids; incompatible_pairs/truth_table rows are raw first-name strings because they are predicate examples and need not correspond to fixture rows.

D1.title: Spill on space, keep together on dash
D1.description: Canonical first keeps dash-bound tokens together, while separate space tokens after the dashed compound still spill into middle; otherwise the first token stays and tokens 2..n spill into middle. This intentionally differs from the current helper's broader keep-all-on-any-dash behavior for mixed dash+space input. Confirms the dash-aware canonical policy (ruled 2026-07-04, per the issue #39 findings: spaced Western firsts are usually first+middle, spaced Chinese compounds are handled upstream, and cross-variant compatibility of Jo / Jo Ann / JoAnn is compare-time via same_prefix_tokens, not canonicalization-identity).

D2.title: Apostrophes stripped globally
D2.description: Apostrophes are removed (not turned into separators) in first, middle, AND last. Legacy strips them only in first; middle/last turn apostrophes into token breaks (O'Brien last -> 'o brien').

D3.title: Uniform apostrophe-like marks
D3.description: All apostrophe-like marks (ASCII ', backtick `, acute, curly quotes, modifier letters, primes, saltillo, fullwidth, and U+FE4D as intentionally inherited from issue #39's apostrophe-like map despite its Unicode name) normalize to nothing in name fields (ruled 2026-07-04). Implementation: unify apostrophe-like code points to ASCII ' before unidecode, then delete ' and ` after unidecode.

D4.title: Dash uniformity
D4.description: All dash-like characters behave identically to one another; no ASCII vs Unicode dash distinction anywhere. For given names dash-bound tokens stay together (see D1); for surnames dash and space variants canonicalize to the same spaced form (see D5).

D5.title: Spaced canonical surnames, spaced count keys
D5.description: Canonical last names are stored as normalized space-separated tokens with particles preserved ('ou yang', 'van der berg'). Canonical count keys use the spaced forms; the compact-join shims (ouyang/vanderberg) are retired.

D6.title: Count keys use canonical fields after gating
D6.description: Count keys use the canonical fields after missing and informativeness gating (no compaction), and keys with a missing component are null (no lookup / NaN feature). This changes live feature values for missing-first examples: legacy still looks up last_first_initial when first is empty (for example lfi key 'smith'), while canonical_v2 suppresses that lookup. Empty-last/null-last are already pinned to null last-dependent legacy keys in the live code, so they are regression guards rather than headline feature changes. The change lands inside the single re-baseline/retrain cycle and is gated by its end-metric non-regression eval. The informative threshold is string-level: first and first_last are suppressed only when the canonical first key has length <= 1. Multi-initial compounds such as 'h g' and joined initials such as 'hg' are intentionally informative; a lone initial such as 'h' is not.

D7.title: Leading title prefixes dropped
D7.description: A single leading NAME_PREFIXES token (dr, prof, ...) is dropped from first, as today. A prefix-only first therefore canonicalizes to empty, and its first-dependent count keys are null per D6 (matches current field behavior).

D8.title: last_first_initial stays initial-char
D8.description: The last_first_initial count key remains '<canonical last> <first initial char>' (initial_char semantics, matching the current default and Arrow contract).

truth_table.notes: A one-token first can be a prefix of a joined expansion.
The aligned tokens must have an exact prefix relation, not edit-distance similarity.
Each aligned token may be an initial-style prefix.
The predicate is prefix compatibility, not semantic identity.
Initials are compatible when every aligned token is a prefix.
A short first name can be a prefix of a longer token; callers must rely on other features too.
A later aligned token mismatch makes the pair incompatible.
